## Dieses Dokument

- Titel: Brief von Lotte Zweig an Hannah; Altmann, Manfred Altmann [April 1941], SZ-AAL/B1.109
- Signatur: SZ-AAL/B1.109
- Datum: 04.1941
- Objekttyp: Brief
- Umfang: 2 Scans

pages.transcription:
Dear Hanna u Manfred
To-day your letter of Feb. 27 last week your letter Nr 4, - there is still one (Nr. 3)
missing, where you apparently wrote about mother and business as I gather
from the other letters. Lots of our letters must be lost or delayed, for I
wrote almost daily in the period where I was settling Eva. Resumé: Eva
had a lovely home at Salmon's, a nicely-furnished modern country house
in beautiful surroundings, S.'s were nice to her and Mr. S. especially
spoiling her as much as he could and taking enormous pains to gain her
love and interest. He overdid this apparently for although they were al-
ways very polite and friendly together there was no real contact. S.'s seemed
to realize this better than Eva who liked being with them but admitted
she was being spoiled and bored. To the head-mistress of the school she was
in, had just said her school was too easy and she had better change over
to another school with higher grades, this was a good opportunity, and I
agreed with S's in all friendship - they were surprisingly nice and
understanding about it, one really shouldn't judge them by their deter-
mined not-writing - that Eva would better be with a lot of other
children and different school. Then, after long deliberations and con-
sultations with all kinds of people, I decided for Schaeffes's place, and
from all we can judge until now, it seems exactly the right thing for Eva,
I wrote you that after all she goes to the Public School now and I must
say I am rather glad things did turn out this way and that she is not
brought up on the super-individualistic methods of the Progressive School,
even if this particular one was supposed to be very good. - Eva looks very
well, unchanged, still a little bit on the stout side but not at all fat, and
is her old self again. As Mrs. Sch. writes she is gay and seems very happy
in her house, is friendly with the other children and there are now
quite a number in her age. The dresses I saw on her fit her perfectly - the
red velvet, the checked dress and the yellow Yella. Mrs. Salmon had got
her a nice new coat (and an awful hat with a feather which fortunately she
need not wear any more) and I bought her for outdoor life in Boston
a ski-suit, wind-and waterproof, blue with a red hood, and a pair of high
rubbers. That was all she needed. She has grown a little, but not too much.
Sch's try to lure her into out-door activities with various tricks. She does
not like that too much yet, probably because she is not used to it and
the others are better in winter sports and games than she is. But that
will change once this long winter is over. We had been longing for
winter weather, but we have already enough, it is too cold and windy to
go out as we can't put on snow suits in the street. - As Stefan wrote you about
my illness, I better report too. I had a bad cold with an asthma-attack, the
first since 2 years, fortunately I got asthma-syn here, and a week later it de-
veloped into a flu. I am very glad for I finally had my necessary fever
again for a few days and this will settle the asthma for months, I suppose.
Poor Stefan has been very patient and helpful and hardly at all a "Jewish nurse"
but as usual the fact that I was not available for work has made him more
anxious to work than usual.

[Randnotiz links:]
I will see what I can do about the
affidavit. It is very difficult and best luck
Thanks address now.
